name: Murukku
subtitle: spiralled rice flour crisps, the snack tin that is never empty

ingredients.note: the roasted dal is what makes it crisp rather than hard
or ghee; the fat is what stops it being a jaw-breaker

prepNotes: The dough should be soft enough to press and stiff enough to hold a spiral. Too soft and it breaks in the oil.
Fry on steady medium. High heat browns the outside while the inside stays raw and chewy.

steps.text: Dry roast the urad dal until it smells nutty and turns pale gold, cool, and grind to a fine flour.
Mix both flours with the sesame, cumin, asafoetida, salt and softened butter, rubbing until it resembles crumbs.
Add water a little at a time to a smooth, soft dough. Do not let it get sticky.
Press spirals directly onto a greased sheet using a murukku press with the star plate.
Slide them into medium-hot oil and fry until the bubbling stops and they turn pale gold, about 5 minutes.
steps.tip: When the hissing stops, the water has gone and they are done. Colour alone will mislead you.

steps.text: Drain on paper and cool completely before storing.
steps.tip: Completely. Stored warm they go soft overnight.

storage: Keeps 3 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature. Low moisture is what makes it keep, so seal the tin properly and never refrigerate.
